title: Eldridge Brothers Rhythm Kings in Pittsburgh
summary: After a wire warned him off New York Roy and Joe formed a Pittsburgh band with Kenny Clarke and beat local bands, then left for McKinney's.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money

blocks.x: When you went out with McKinney's, that was after... You left New York then to go out on the road with them.

No, what happened was that... It was a time that I was with Connie's Hot Chocolates on the road. And I got a wire from my buddy telling me, don't come back to New York, they're waiting for me at the station, at the airport, anywhere I'd come in, you know. So I went to Pittsburgh. It was something to do with a chick, I don't know...

Joe drove me to Pittsburgh, and then we formed a band in Pittsburgh called the Eldridge Brothers Rhythm Kings. That was an interesting little thing. We had a gig... Oh, one of the first gigs. But we had a good band.
You were talking about the Eldridge Brothers.
Yeah. Kenny Clarke was in that band.

Yeah. Kenny Clarke extracted(?)... He got my set of drums that I had, you know, what I had from the carnival. After I left, he told my father that I wanted him to have them -- which I never told him that, you know.
Was he a friend of the family?

No! He was just in the band. Oh, we played a battle around there, you know, with all the local bands -- the Milford(?) Brothers and the Harlemites and...I can't think of the others. These were the big names out of Pittsburgh, you know. And we wiped all of them out. Wiped them out. But then there was a bad thing, because then all of a sudden the cats in the band got the big head. I'd never seen cats get the big head about winning a contest with no money involved. We had a job that was paying about eight dollars a night, or a week or something like that, not a night... But they really did... They got strung out, man. All of a sudden they were big shots.

So we got this offer to go to Baltimore to join McKinney's Cotton Pickers, and we left the band.
